title: Customer data migration and acceptance playbook for private deployments
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the end-to-end process, runbook steps, verification checks, and rollback strategies for migrating customer data (model artifacts, KV caches, tenant metadata, and telemetry pointers) into Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is written for field engineers, customer success leads, and SREs involved in a migration engagement.

Scope
- Applies to private deployments delivered by Redwood (VPC-hosted private control plane and fully on-prem bundles).
- Covers: data export from source environment, transfer packaging, validation, staged import, acceptance testing, and coordinated rollback.
- Excludes: deep schema changes to customer application databases (coordinate separately with customer DB team).

Owners and stakeholders
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Ava Martinez)
- Primary implementers: Field Ops / Deployment Engineers
- SRE support: Platform Oncall for migration window (pager)
- Security reviewer: Security & Compliance (must approve transport plan if customer data classified sensitive)
- Customer primary: named contact in onboarding ticket

Pre-migration checklist (must be green before any data movement)
1) Acceptance window scheduled and approved by customer and Redwood PM.
2) Signed data transfer agreement if data classification is PII/sensitive.
3) Snapshot retention policy agreed (number of backups, retention TTL).
4) Capacity reservation: GPU/CPU, storage, egress bandwidth verified.
5) Key rotation/crypto plan approved for transit (TLS + signed manifests).
6) Test tenant created in target environment and smoke-tested.
7) Monitoring & tracing hooks instrumented in target (request/response latency, KV miss/hit, token accounting).

High-level migration phases
1. Plan & dry-run
2. Export & package
3. Transfer & verify integrity
4. Staged import to test tenant
5. Functional verification & acceptance tests
6. Cutover to production tenant
7. Post-migration monitoring and cleanup

Detailed runbook steps
Phase 1 — Plan & dry-run (owner: Customer Success + Field Ops)\- Confirm data components to migrate: model files (weights), tokenizer and vocab, KV cache snapshots, tenant metadata (routing rules, quotas), eval/quality baselines, telemetry pointers.\- Produce a Migration Plan doc: file inventory, expected sizes, checksums, transfer windows, and rollback points.\- Perform a dry-run with a 10% subset of data into a test tenant. Capture timings and failure modes.

Phase 2 — Export & package (owner: Customer Success / Customer IT)\- Recommended export format: gzipped tarball with a signed manifest.json that includes sha256 checksums and schema version. Example manifest entry:
  {
    "path": "models/llama-v2-7b/weights.pt",
    "sha256": "<hex>",
    "size_bytes": "123456789",
    "type": "model"
  }
- For KV caches: produce both a flat snapshot and an incremental WAL if supported. Label snapshot with sequence ID.
- Encryption: use customer-provided KMS envelope encryption or PKCS7 with our field tooling. Transport keys are rotated per migration.

Phase 3 — Transfer & verify integrity (owner: Field Ops)\- Transfer options (choose based on environment):
  - Secure SFTP (for on-prem to Redwood VPC) with IP allowlist
  - HTTPS multipart upload to pre-signed target bucket (for VPC-hosted private control plane)
  - Physical shipment for extremely large datasets (follow hardware courier runbook)
- Verification steps: validate manifest signatures, verify sha256 for each file. Any mismatch: quarantined and re-requested from source.

Phase 4 — Staged import to test tenant (owner: Field Ops + Runtime Team)\- Import order (strict):
  1) Tenant metadata and routing rules (so services know where to route requests)
  2) Model artifacts (weights + tokenizer) — register model in model-catalog with provisional version tag
  3) KV cache snapshots — load as read-only first, warm-up using background rehydrate jobs
  4) Eval baseline and quality checks (register prompt sets and expected metrics)\- Runtime flags to use during staged import: 
  - --model-register-mode=provisional
  - --kv-load-mode=readonly
  - --rehydrate-workers=4
  - --disable-autoscaler=true

Phase 5 — Functional verification & acceptance tests (owner: Customer Success + QA)
- Test categories and example checks:
  - Connectivity: ping endpoints, validate TLS cert chain.
  - Authentication: token exchange flow for customer's IAM integration.
  - Model correctness: canonical prompt set (20–50 items) should return matching outputs within quality tolerance thresholds.
  - Latency & throughput: 95th percentile latency must be within agreed SLO delta vs baseline (table below).
  - KV cache hit rate: expected warm hit rate > 60% within 2 hours of warm-up.
  - Billing / metering: per-token accounting sanity check against simulated traffic.

Acceptance criteria table
| Signal | Requirement | Measurement window | Action if fail |
|--------|-------------|--------------------|----------------|
|Model functional pass rate| >= 95% on canonical prompts| 1 hour | Fail and rollback to last stable model|
|95p latency delta| +<20% vs baseline| 1 hour | Investigate autoscaler and routing|
|KV cache warm hit rate| >= 60% within 2 hours| 2 hours | Trigger background rehydrate, extend warm window|
|Telemetry completeness| >99% traces & metrics ingested| 30 minutes| Re-check ingestion pipeline and backfill missing spans|
|Metering reconciliation| <1% token accounting drift| 24 hours| Start billing investigation and hold invoices|

Phase 6 — Cutover to production tenant (owner: Field Ops + SRE)\- Pre-cutover checklist: all acceptance tests green; snapshot of test and pre-production manifests archived; rollback snapshot taken and hash-signed.\- Cutover method options:
  1) DNS switch / routing table update to point traffic at new tenant (preferred for VPC control plane)
  2) Blue/Green tenant swap using the platform’s tenant-routing feature
  3) Gradual traffic ramp using percentage-based routing (canary)
- Cutover steps (canary example):
  1) Route 1% traffic for 10 minutes. Monitor critical signals (errors, latency, model outputs).
  2) If green, increase to 10% for 20 minutes.
  3) Continue 25% -> 50% -> 100% with at least two monitoring windows per step.
- Post-cutover: mark provisional model versions as active and update model-catalog and billing tags.

Phase 7 — Post-migration monitoring and cleanup (owner: SRE + Customer Success)\- Minimum 72-hour elevated monitoring with daily sync calls.\- Run sanity reconciliation jobs: metric comparison, token billing reconciliation, config drift checks.
- Clean up provisional artifacts after 30 days if no issues (automatically archive).

Rollback strategies and safe abort points
- Abort during transfer: stop imports and request re-transfer; no state change in target.
- Abort after staged import but before cutover: mark import as quarantined and keep imports read-only; restore previous routing.
- Abort during canary: immediately shift traffic back to previous tenant and mark the incident for postmortem.
- Full rollback: use the pre-cutover snapshot manifest to restore model catalog and KV snapshots. Restoration checklist:
  - Verify restoration manifest checksums.
  - Re-enable autoscaler and health checks.
  - Communicate with customer and open a rollback RCA ticket.

Operational tooling and commands (examples)
- Verify manifest sha256:
  cat manifest.json | jq -c '.files[]' | while read f; do sha256sum "$(echo $f | jq -r .path)" | grep "$(echo $f | jq -r .sha256)" || echo "mismatch:$f"; done
- Import model (field CLI):
  redwoodctl model import --tenant $TENANT --path models/llama-v2-7b/weights.pt --tag provisional-2026-03-15
- Load KV snapshot as readonly:
  redwoodctl kv load --tenant $TENANT --snapshot kv-20260315.tar.gz --mode readonly

Telemetry & observable signals to watch (real-time)
- Request error rate (5xx and internal errors)
- Model output regression signals (semantic drift detector events)
- KV cache miss ratio and rehydrate job backlog
- Autoscaler activity and container restart rate
- Token accounting deltas between gateway and billing service
- Ingestion lag for traces/metrics (should be < 60s for critical spans)

Security and compliance considerations
- Ensure all transfer endpoints are in allowlists and logs retained per retention policy.
- For regulated customers, ensure audit events are exported to customer SIEM (via syslog or secure forwarder).
- If migration includes customer secrets, use HSM-backed envelope keys; log key usage to audit trail.

Rollforward and incremental migration pattern (when dataset too large)
- Use incremental WAL + snapshot approach: seed with a full snapshot, then apply ordered WAL batches until cutover window.
- Validate ordering invariants by sequence numbers in manifests and ensure idempotency by consumer.

Common failure modes and remediation (quick reference)
- Mismatch checksums: re-run export, verify source FS integrity.
- Slow rehydrate: increase rehydrate-workers, or temporarily route low-latency traffic to model variant without cache dependency.
- Hidden model regressions: run a wider evaluation prompt set and if failures exceed threshold, rollback model and start postmortem.

Communication plan
- Pre-migration: share schedule and expected customer impact with all stakeholders 72 hours in advance.
- During migration: hourly updates to customer during critical windows; immediate alert on any failed acceptance gate.
- Post migration: 72-hour handoff call, weekly summary for first 30 days.

Appendices
A) Minimal technical artifact checklist (table)\| Artifact | Required | Example path | Notes |
| Model weights | yes | models/llama-v2-7b/weights.pt | Prefer quantized artifacts if customer uses reduced footprint |
| Tokenizer | yes | models/llama-v2-7b/tokenizer.json | Must match model hash |
| KV snapshot | conditional | kv-snapshots/tenant-20260315.tar.gz | Include WAL batches if >0 |
| Manifest | yes | manifest.json | Signed and sha256-verified |

B) Escalation matrix
- Field Ops lead -> SRE oncall -> Platform Engineering -> Head of Customer Success -> Security (if sensitive data)

C) Related runbooks and reference pages
- Post-installation telemetry and acceptance checklist (see related pages)
- Incremental stateful upgrade strategy
